deal: Calderwood Bank is lending to a car finance company, secured on its car loans.
intake: First, the paperwork arrives. The AI sorts it and notices a page is missing.
terms: Next, the key terms. The AI reads each one and points to where it found it.
ontology: The AI understands lending terms, because it is grounded in Artizent's ontology.
facility: Code checks every answer. This one came from a blurry scan, so it is flagged.
amended: This term was changed by a later amendment. The new value is already applied.
bulk: The routine terms are approved together. A person signs off every one.
rules: Then the AI turns the agreement's tests into rules a system can run.
ruleEdit: Anyone changing a rule sees its effect first, and someone else must agree.
mapping: The AI matches the borrower's loan file to the bank's own fields.
validation: Now the real check. No AI here: code tests every loan, to the cent.
bridge: The borrower claimed more than it should. Every dollar of the gap is explained.
drill: Some cars appear twice. The same car may have been used for two loans.
queue: Anything doubtful goes to one place. The analyst decides what happens to each.
sunrise: One dealer was spelled two ways. Counted together, it breaks a limit.
approve: Then sign-off. The analyst who did the work can't approve it.
reviewer: A second analyst reviews every change, then approves.
approved: The loan is ready to watch, with a record of everything that was done.
results: The result: every real problem found, and nothing harmless flagged.
